title: Task Assignment with Interdependent Incentives
abstract: arXiv:2511.05338v5 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We study a manager's repeated assignment of a burden among a group of homogeneous workers under imperfect public monitoring of workers' effort. Their effort incentives are interdependent because assignment is exclusive. We develop recursive bounds on workers' assignment frequencies to address this interdependence and characterize the manager's optimum among equilibria inducing effort whenever assignment occurs. We also explicitly construct an equilibrium attaining this optimum. Whenever some effortful assignment is sustainable, this equilibrium retains the assignee after failure and relieves him after success until each other worker has produced a success and a vacancy phase has elapsed. Our results extend to assignment of a desirable task.

translated_title: 相互依赖激励下的任务分配
translated_abstract: 我们研究了在工人努力程度受到不完美公共监督的条件下，管理者如何在一组同质工人之间重复分配负担的问题。由于分配具有排他性，工人的努力激励是相互依赖的。为处理这种相互依赖性，我们推导了工人被分配频率的递归边界，并刻画了在所有能在分配发生时激励努力的均衡中管理者的最优选择。我们还显式构造了达到该最优结果的均衡。只要某种需要努力的分配是可持续的，该均衡在失败后保留被分配者，在成功后解除其任务，直到其他每个工人都各产生一次成功且经过一个空缺阶段。我们的结果还可推广至理想任务的分配。
tldr: 该论文针对排他性任务分配导致的激励相互依赖问题，通过递归边界刻画了管理者在重复分配中的最优均衡，并显式构造了“失败后保留、成功后轮换”的最优分配规则。
en_tdlr: This paper addresses interdependent incentives in repeated exclusive task assignment by developing recursive bounds on assignment frequencies, characterizing the manager's optimal equilibrium, and explicitly constructing an equilibrium featuring retention after failure and rotation after success.
